options: A replacement for Scheduled Jobs with no connection to ATF
A single Test Step that cannot be reused across different Tests
A record that stores only UI Tests, never server-side Tests
A grouping of multiple individual Tests that run together as one coordinated set, with one combined result
questions.explain: A Test Suite groups related individual Tests so they run together and report a single pass/fail result.

questions.q: What is the deeper value of grouping related Tests into a Suite, beyond convenience?
options: A Suite removes the need for verification steps inside any of its Tests
Grouping has no real benefit over running Tests one at a time
A change rarely affects just one narrow scenario, so running the whole related group together is what actually makes regression testing practical at scale
Grouping Tests makes each individual Test run faster on its own
questions.explain: A Business Rule change on one table can affect several related workflows at once, so the related Tests need to run together.

options: Automated running of a Test Suite on a defined, recurring schedule, the same underlying idea as Course 3's Scheduled Jobs
A way to permanently delete old Test results
A feature that only works for server-side Tests, never UI Tests
A manual process where an admin clicks "Run Test" once per quarter
questions.explain: It's a server-side task that fires on its own schedule with no user present to trigger it, just like a Scheduled Job.

questions.q: Why does scheduling a Test Suite to run nightly matter, according to this lesson?
options: It catches a regression the very next night as a failed Test result, rather than weeks later from a support ticket after a real user hits it in production
It guarantees that no Business Rule will ever be changed again
It only matters for Tests that already passed previously
It replaces the need to write any Test Steps at all
questions.explain: A nightly scheduled run surfaces a regression close to when it was introduced, rather than relying on someone remembering to test manually.

questions.q: What problem from Lesson 12 does a scheduled Test Suite run most directly close?
options: The problem of forms rendering too slowly during a UI Test
The risk that a silent regression goes undetected simply because nobody manually triggered a test run that day
The problem of application scopes colliding with the Global scope
The problem of Script Includes being difficult to write
questions.explain: Lesson 12 opened the chapter with silent, undetected regressions; a scheduled run means testing happens even on days nobody thinks about it.
